name: inprocess-obi-apb-pulp-i2c-two-step-clear-f5
notes: PULP apb_i2c real level interrupt (configs/peripherals/pulp_i2c_irq), same trigger as the single-clear scenario: CTRL=0xc0 (core_en|ien), TX=0x5a, CMD=0x10 (write); STATUS[0] is the cause.

The declared clear is the device's ordered two-write acknowledge sequence, stated as the executor key irq_clear_sequence=[[20,1],[20,0]] (CMD=1 then CMD=0). The behavior file configs/behaviors/pulp_i2c_level_two_step_f5.json documents the RTL facts; it states no clear_writes of its own because the sequence is one declaration, and this increment's behavior-schema layer still bounds its own clear_sequence fact to one step, so the executor owns the ordered form.

RTL facts: apb_i2c.sv:128 `wire iack = r_cmd[0];` (the acknowledge is a held register bit) and apb_i2c.sv:189-193 `irq_flag <= (s_done | i2c_al | irq_flag) & ~iack;`. The first write clears irq_flag and interrupt_o = irq_flag && s_ien drops; the second write releases the held iack so the device is not left masking every later s_done.

The F5 handler reads STATUS (0xc), performs CMD=1 then CMD=0, and stores the status word it read. A handler that performed only the first write fails the clear count; one that performed the writes out of order fails the ordered classification in the host. The device is left with iack=0, so the reported final raw level must be low.
This file declares the scenario; the real RTL run under runs/p1-irq/ is the evidence.
